title: Returning a Found Item
instructions: Speak about a real or imagined found item and use feedback to improve your original recording.
prompt: Describe a real or imagined item you find in a public place. Explain where it is, whom you ask for help, what you do with it, and one reason for your choice. Give one polite request. Speak for about 75–105 seconds. Explain who two objects belong to, using a possessive expression and an object pronoun.
reference: I find a small bag near the office door. I do not know who the owner is, so I take it to the office worker. I can ask, “Could you keep this bag until its owner comes back, please?” The worker can record the items and tell visitors where to ask. I choose the office because it is a clear public place for lost things. If I need to leave, I will tell the worker where I found the bag. If I find a bag, I give it to a worker. I ask whose bag it is instead of showing every item to visitors. The worker can ask the owner to describe it. My own bag has a green jacket inside, so I can say that the jacket is mine.
